statement: For 2020 KTM split the 85 SX into the 17/14 (small wheel) and a new 19/16 (big wheel) model; both got a muffler with new packing that saves 40 g, while the engine (47 x 48.95 mm, Keihin PWK 28, kick start, 6-speed, hydraulic clutch) and the WP XACT air fork / linkless PDS shock chassis carried over.
notes: Magazine first look relaying KTM launch information; the owner's manual lists the same engine and chassis data.

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling - 2020 KTM Mini Motocrossers First Look (7 Fast Facts)

statement: For 2021 the 85 SX got new Formula brakes with a two-piston front and one-piston rear caliper using the same pads as KTM's big bikes, a 220 mm rear disc (up from 210 mm) on a new hub, and a roller-type throttle with new cable, plus new graphics.
notes: Magazine first look relaying KTM information; confirmed by the 2020 vs 2021 owner's manuals (below).

source.name: Ultimate Motorcycling - 2021 KTM Youth Motocross Lineup First Look

topic: 2021 85 SX changes in the owner's manual
statement: KTM's 2021 85 SX owner's manual differs from 2020 in: front brake caliper 4-piston to 2-piston, rear 2-piston to 1-piston, rear disc 210 to 220 mm; shock listed as WP XACT 5746 (was 5743) with new fork and shock article numbers; shock high-speed compression presets now Comfort 2.5 / Standard 2 / Sport 1.5 turns (2020 listed 1.5 / 2 / 2.5).
notes: Field-by-field comparison of the technical-data chapters of the 2020 and 2021 manuals; wording-only changes ignored.

source.name: KTM Owner's Manual 2021 85 SX, item no. 3214206en (compared with the 2020 manual)

statement: KTM's 2022 85 SX owner's manual technical data match the 2021 manual (same engine, gearing, chassis, brakes, fork and shock data); the only addition is the 5 bar (73 psi) standard fork air pressure printed in the fork table.
notes: Comparison of the 2021 and 2022 manuals.

source.name: KTM Owner's Manual 2022 85 SX, item no. 3214408en (compared with the 2021 manual)

statement: KTM's 2023 85 SX owner's manual technical data are identical to the 2022 manual, so the 2023 bike is a carry-over of the 2018-generation 85 SX with the 2021 brake update.
notes: Comparison of the 2022 and 2023 manuals.

source.name: KTM Owner's Manual 2023 85 SX, item no. 3214636en (compared with the 2022 manual)

statement: KTM's 2024 85 SX owner's manual technical data are identical to 2023 apart from wording; 2024 is the last year of the 2018-2024 85 SX generation before the 2025 redesign.
notes: Comparison of the 2023 and 2024 manuals; the 2025 manual shows the new chassis and engine changes.

source.name: KTM Owner's Manual 2024 85 SX, item no. 3214830en (compared with the 2023 manual)

statement: KTM's 2024 85 SX page describes the carry-over package: Keihin PWK 28 flat-slide carburetor, an exhaust control drum with an adjusting screw for its opening point, a modified clutch with Formula hydraulics that self-adjusts for wear, a silencer with damping material 40 g lighter, chromoly frame with aluminium subframe, cast swingarm, WP XACT AER fork and PDS shock (305 mm travel), 5.2 l tank and 67 kg without fuel (17/14).
notes: The page also prints four-piston/two-piston Formula brakes and calls the fork "WP XACT 43" in its spec list; the 2021-2024 owner's manuals list 2-piston front / 1-piston rear calipers, so the page copy looks outdated on those points.

source.name: KTM Austria model page - 2024 KTM 85 SX 17/14

statement: The 2025 85 SX is a new generation: new cylinder head, spark plug, ignition, exhaust and shift drum with revised carburetor settings for more low and mid-range power and torque; new chromoly frame, one-piece polyamide/aluminium subframe and a one-piece cast swingarm 300 g lighter with a 20 mm rear axle; head angle 63.5 degrees (half a degree flatter, 6 mm further back), 35 degree steering lock, engine rotated 3 degrees up; a new, more compact WP XACT linkless shock with travel cut from 305 to 289 mm; the same 43 mm XACT AER fork at 4.8 bar instead of 5.0; slimmer bodywork, larger radiators.
notes: Magazine article relaying KTM's 2025 release.

source.name: Australasian Dirt Bike - 2025 KTM 85 SX revealed

topic: 2025 85 SX changes in the owner's manual
statement: KTM's 2025 85 SX owner's manual versus 2024: steering head 66 to 63.5 degrees, wheelbase 1,290 to 1,282 mm, rear travel 305 to 289 mm, seat 865 to 845 mm (17/14) and 890 to 871 mm (19/16), ground clearance 336 to 308 mm (17/14), idle 1,400-1,500 to 1,500-2,000 rpm, plug NGK BR9 ECMVX to BRISK AR10C (0.70 mm gap), standard jets main 142 to 140 and idle 48 to 55, shock springs now 40/45/50 N/mm for under 40 / 40-50 / over 50 kg riders (was 35/40/45 for under 45 / 45-55 / over 55 kg), rider sag 120 to 100 mm, fork air 5.0 to 4.8 bar.
notes: Comparison of the 2024 and 2025 manuals.

source.name: KTM Owner's Manual 2025 85 SX, item no. 3240038en (compared with the 2024 manual)

statement: KTM's 2026 85 SX owner's manual repeats the 2025 technical data (engine, carburetor settings, gearing, chassis, fork and shock) with only formatting changes, so the 2026 85 SX carries over the 2025 generation.
notes: Comparison of the 2025 and 2026 manuals. The piston-to-cylinder X dimension is printed as 0.00-0.10 mm in 2026 but 2.10-2.20 mm in 2025 and 2027; see conflicts.

source.name: KTM Owner's Manual 2026 85 SX, item no. 3240229en (compared with the 2025 manual)

statement: KTM's 2027 85 SX owner's manual repeats the 2026 technical data (engine, Keihin PWK 28 settings, 13:46 / 13:49 final drive, chassis, fork and shock) apart from the X-dimension print and a shock-oil line, which matches KTM publishing only new graphics for the 2027 85 SX.
notes: Comparison of the 2026 and 2027 manuals.

source.name: KTM Owner's Manual 2027 85 SX, item no. 3240375en (compared with the 2026 manual)

statement: KTM says the 2025 85 SX engine update (new head, plug, ignition and exhaust with revised carburetor settings) gives more power in the low and mid-rpm range and more torque than the previous generation; no power figure is published.
notes: Applied to 2026-2027 because the owner's manuals list identical engine and carburetor data for 2025, 2026 and 2027.

source.name: Australasian Dirt Bike - 2025 KTM 85 SX revealed

statement: In a 2025 85cc comparison the KTM-group 85s were stronger off the bottom and on top than the 2024 version and considerably stronger than the YZ85 and KX85; the engine is made to rev, recovers well from a bobble, and the KTM/GasGas version (open airbox) pulled longer and ran leaner than the Husqvarna with its closed airbox. Four of five testers picked the KTM-group 85 as the best bike.
notes: Qualitative test-rider impressions, no dyno numbers published. Applied to 2026-2027 because the manuals show the same engine data.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2025 MXA 85cc shootout (Yamaha vs Husqvarna vs GasGas vs Kawasaki vs KTM)

statement: A 2025 race test of the KTM-group 85 (identical apart from colour, brand and bodywork) found it pulls harder off the bottom and transitions smoothly into the midrange while keeping the top-end snap, where the 2024 bike was lazy off the bottom; testers called it a smarter rather than a stronger engine.
notes: Test of the GasGas MC 85 17/14, which the magazine says is the same bike as the KTM 85 SX apart from colour, brand and bodywork.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test of the 2025 GasGas MC85

topic: 2025+ 85 SX test complaints: jetting and plastics
statement: Testers found the stock Keihin PWK 28 jetting rich (oil residue on the silencer, a slight midrange flat spot); with KTM R&D they kept the 140 main, dropped to a 42 pilot and used the NRJC needle in the 3rd clip with the air screw 1.5 turns out. Rigid plastic fenders snapped in crashes, the side panels hide the shock clickers (GasGas marks where to drill an access hole), the seat cover was slippery and the air fork needs its pressure checked before every ride.
notes: Race test of the identical GasGas MC 85; jetting change is the testers' working setup, not an OEM spec.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test of the 2025 GasGas MC85

topic: 2025+ 85 SX test complaints: ergonomics and brakes
statement: In a 2025 85cc comparison testers wanted taller handlebars, drilled the shrouds to reach the shock clickers, broke a rear fender in a small crash, found the Formula brakes weaker than the Brembos on KTM's big bikes (Brembo parts fit without issue for fast riders) and found the steering lock tight in the pits and on tight trails.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2025 MXA 85cc shootout (Yamaha vs Husqvarna vs GasGas vs Kawasaki vs KTM)

statement: Testers running the 2025 KTM-group 85 at sea level leaned the stock jetting: one setup used a 142 main, 52 pilot and needle clip 3 (stock listed as 145 main, 55 pilot, clip 3, air screw 1.5 out, slightly fat), another kept the 140 main with a 42 pilot and NRJC needle in clip 3 after consulting KTM R&D; both cleaned up the rich midrange.
notes: Two magazine tests report different stock main jets (145 in the shootout, 140 in the owner's manual and race test); the owner's manual standard is 140 main / 55 idle jet. Jetting must suit altitude and temperature (the manual carries a full chart).

source.name: Motocross Action - 2025 MXA 85cc shootout (Yamaha vs Husqvarna vs GasGas vs Kawasaki vs KTM)

statement: KTM PowerParts lists an FMF Factory Fatty pipe (A41005907001, about $300) with matching FMF Turbine Core 2 and Powercore 2 silencers for the 2025-2027 85 SX, and a tuner sells a Works pipe for the 2025-on KTM/Husqvarna/GasGas 85; the 2018-2024 85 pipes do not carry over to the new 2025 chassis listings.
notes: Dealer listing of the PowerParts item; no power figures are claimed. A tuner 2025 listing: https://www.revzilla.com/dirt-bike/pro-circuit-works-pipe-ktm-husqvarna-gas-gas-85cc-2025

source.name: AOMC - KTM/HQV/GG FMF Factory Fatty pipe 85 SX 25-27 (PowerParts A41005907001)

statement: A tuner lists its Works pipe for the 2018-2024 KTM/Husqvarna/GasGas 85cc generation (about $320), claiming more usable power; no figures are given.
notes: Listing title says 2018-2024 while the URL says 2018-2022.

source.name: RevZilla - Pro Circuit Works pipe KTM/Husqvarna/GasGas 85cc 2018-2024

statement: A race test of the 2018-generation 85 SX (unchanged in engine and chassis through 2024) disliked the soft plastic shock preload ring (testers pry it round instead of using a punch), the power-valve adjuster that needs a Robertson (square) wrench, the #15 Torx fork bleed screw, a hard-to-remove airbox side cover, and a small hard bar pad.
notes: 2018 test; the 2020-2024 owner's manuals list the same engine, frame and suspension data, with only the 2021 brake update.

source.name: Motocross Action - Race test 2018 KTM 85SX

statement: KTM's 2027 SX range brings a revised colour and in-mould graphics package with more orange and red on the tank spoilers and "refined engine packages" meeting current FIM noise rules; the hydroformed, laser-cut, robot-welded chromoly frame architecture continues, as do WP XACT suspension, Pankl gearboxes, Dunlop Geomax MX34 tires, Excel rims, Brembo brakes and clutches, Neken bars and Keihin throttle bodies. Minis reach Australian dealers from June 2026, full-size models from July 2026.
notes: Magazine article relaying KTM's 2027 release; no model-specific technical changes are listed.

source.name: Australasian Dirt Bike - KTM unveils 2027 SX motocross range

statement: KTM's 2027 125 SX owner's manual technical data match the 2026 manual (engine, gearing 13:50, chassis, WP XACT AER fork with 8.4/8.6/8.8 bar by rider weight, XACT LDS shock with 36/39/42 N/mm springs); the 2027 manual only adds the 14 V / 77 W alternator line and the fork grease quantity.
notes: Comparison of the 2026 and 2027 manuals.

source.name: KTM Owner's Manual 2027 125 SX / 125 XC, item no. 3240379en (compared with 2026 manual 3240232en)

statement: KTM lists the 2027 125 SX with Keihin electronic fuel injection through a 39 mm throttle body, managed by a Vitesco Technologies EMS.

source.name: KTM Italy technical specifications - 2027 KTM 125 SX

statement: KTM's 2027 125 SX spec sheet: 25CrMo4 central double-cradle frame, aluminium-reinforced polyamide subframe, 48 mm WP XACT AER fork and WP XACT linkage shock with 310/300 mm travel, 958 mm seat, 359 mm ground clearance, 7.2 l tank, 92 kg without fuel, non-sealed 520 chain.

source.name: KTM Italy technical specifications - 2027 KTM 125 SX

statement: KTM's 2027 250 SX-F owner's manual repeats the 2026 US-model technical data except the weight without fuel, now 101.5 kg for EU and US bikes (the 2026 US standard model was listed at 101 kg).
notes: Comparison of the 2026 and 2027 manuals.

source.name: KTM Owner's Manual 2027 250 SX-F / 250 XC-F, item no. 3240381en (compared with 2026 manual 3240234en)

topic: 2027 US SX-F intake spec for sound rules
statement: KTM's PowerParts fitting notes for its Akrapovic exhausts say US MY27 standard SX-F models (like EU MY26 and US MY26 Factory Editions) use a different airbox and air filter: to fit the race exhaust the airbox and filter must be changed back to MY25 parts and the matching engine map installed, after which the bike no longer meets the 109 dB FIM limit.
notes: Installation note on the dealer listing of KTM PowerParts a dealer (250) and A48005900044 (450). It shows the 2027 US engine "updates for sound regulations" include intake changes.

source.name: AOMC - KTM/HQV/GG Akrapovic Slip-On Line 250 SX-F/XC-F 23-27 (A46005979000)

statement: KTM's 2027 350 SX-F owner's manual matches the 2026 US data except: one weight of 102.4 kg for all SX-F models (2026 US: 101.9 kg), chain listed as 520 (same size as the 5/8 x 1/4 in previously printed) and rear sprocket options 50 and 52 teeth.
notes: Comparison of the 2026 and 2027 manuals.

source.name: KTM Owner's Manual 2027 350 SX-F / 350 XC-F, item no. 3240383en (compared with 2026 manual 3240235en)

statement: KTM's 2027 350 SX-F page lists no 2027-specific changes beyond the frame updates carried from KTM Factory Racing input (streamlined shock-mount area, optimised engine mounts, flex cut-outs); its engine text still refers to the 2025 350 SX-F engine and the threaded radiator cap is labelled as a 2026 change.

source.name: KTM model page - 2027 KTM 350 SX-F

statement: KTM's 2027 450 SX-F owner's manual technical data for the US model are identical to the 2026 manual: 95 x 63.4 mm, 13.6:1, 29:72 primary, 13:51 final drive, 120/80-19 rear tire, 103.2 kg without fuel, fork air 10.3/10.5/10.7 bar and 42/45/48 N/mm shock springs by rider weight.
notes: Comparison of the 2026 and 2027 manuals.

source.name: KTM Owner's Manual 2027 450 SX-F / 450 XC-F, item no. 3240384en (compared with 2026 manual 3240236en)

statement: KTM's 2027 250 SX-F spec sheet: 249.9 cc with Keihin EFI (44 mm throttle body) and Keihin EMS, 24:72 primary, hydraulic Brembo DS clutch, 5-speed, 25CrMo4 frame with polyamide/aluminium subframe, 48 mm WP XACT AER fork and XACT shock (310/300 mm), 958 mm seat, 343 mm ground clearance, 7.2 l tank, 101.5 kg without fuel, 520 chain.

source.name: KTM Italy technical specifications - 2027 KTM 250 SX-F

statement: KTM describes the 2027 350 SX-F engine as giving usable power through the rev range from a 27.5 kg (60.6 lb) engine; map 1 is the more linear power curve and map 2 more aggressive, with traction control on the same switch.
notes: Maker description; no power figure published.

source.name: KTM model page - 2027 KTM 350 SX-F

statement: KTM describes the 2027 450 SX-F as a SOHC single tilted 2 degrees back with a 59 lb engine, and says its silencer gives improved response together with the map switch (map 1 linear, map 2 aggressive); no power figure is published.

source.name: KTM model page - 2027 KTM 450 SX-F

statement: KTM offers the Connectivity Unit Offroad as a PowerPart for the 2027 SX-F: linked to the KTMconnect app it lets the rider adjust engine behaviour (and suspension notes) on top of the two maps, traction control, launch control and quickshifter fitted as standard.
notes: The 450 SX-F CUO is covered elsewhere.

source.name: KTM model page - 2027 KTM 350 SX-F

statement: KTM/Husqvarna/GasGas PowerParts list the titanium Akrapovic Evolution Line full system (a dealer, about $1,670) for 2023-2027 450 SX-F/XC-F, claimed 0.9 kg (23.8%) lighter than stock with better power delivery and throttle response and AMA amateur approval; on GasGas the stock mounting parts are reused, and on US MY27 standard bikes the airbox and filter must go back to MY25 parts with the matching map, after which the bike exceeds the 109 dB FIM limit.
notes: Dealer listing of the PowerParts item; performance claims are not quantified.

source.name: AOMC - KTM/HQV/GG PowerParts Akrapovic Evolution Line 450 SX-F/XC-F 23-27 (A48005900044)

statement: PowerParts also list an FMF Factory 4.1 RCT titanium/carbon silencer (a dealer, about $855) for 2023-2027 450 SX-F/a dealer/XCF-W including Husqvarna and GasGas; it works with the stock header or an FMF Megabomb header, with torque gains claimed but not quantified.
notes: The listing is inconsistent on years (title 23-27, page title 23-25); confirm fitment.

source.name: AOMC - KTM/HQV/GG FMF Factory 4.1 RCT silencer 450 SX-F/XC-F/XCF-W 23-27 (A48005979003)

statement: PowerParts list the Akrapovic Evolution Line full system (a dealer, about $1,670) for 2023-2027 KTM, Husqvarna and GasGas 250/350 SX-F/XC-F.
notes: Dealer listing; no performance figures given.

source.name: AOMC - KTM/HQV/GG Akrapovic Evolution Line 250/350 SX-F/XC-F 23-27 (A46005900044)

statement: PowerParts list a titanium Akrapovic Slip-On Line silencer (a dealer, about $900, FIM noise compliant) for 2023-2027 250 SX-F/XC-F; GasGas bikes reuse the stock mounts, and US MY27 standard models need the MY25 airbox, filter and map to run it, which takes them over the 109 dB FIM limit.
notes: Dealer listing reproducing the PowerParts fitting note.

source.name: AOMC - KTM/HQV/GG Akrapovic Slip-On Line 250 SX-F/XC-F 23-27 (A46005979000)

statement: PowerParts list an FMF Factory 4.1 RCT titanium silencer with carbon cap (a dealer, about $675) for 2023-2027 SX-F/XC-F models.
notes: Listing title says 23-27, meta text says 23-26; confirm fitment.

source.name: AOMC - KTM/HQV/GG FMF Factory 4.1 RCT silencer SX-F/XC-F 23-27 (A46005981003)

statement: Husqvarna's 2027 motocross range has no real technical update: new minimalist Swedish graphics, chromoly frames powder-coated white, a one-piece tank side panel without the small shock-adjuster cover, a fine re-tune of the WP XACT units, and unchanged electronics (two maps, quickshifter, traction and launch control on the four-strokes).
notes: Magazine first ride relaying Husqvarna's launch information; prices in Italy from EUR 9,950 (TC 125) to EUR 12,090 (FC 450).

source.name: InMoto.it - Test Husqvarna Cross 2027 (first ride, Cadrezzate)

statement: Husqvarna lists the 2027 FC 250 at 249.9 cc (81 x 48.5 mm, 14.5:1, DOHC with finger followers), FC 350 at 349.7 cc (88 x 57.5 mm, 14.6:1, DOHC) and FC 450 at 449.9 cc (95 x 63.4 mm, 13.6:1, SOHC with rocker arm), all with Keihin EFI through a 44 mm throttle body and two oil pumps; engines were refined for rideability and current AMA/FIM sound rules.
notes: Magazine spec table relaying Husqvarna data; matches the 2027 owner's manuals.

source.name: Cycle News - 2027 Husqvarna FC motocrossers specs and prices

statement: Husqvarna's 2027 FC spec sheet: FC 250 primary 24:72, gears 13:32, 16:32, 17:28, 19:26, 21:25, final 14:51; FC 350 primary 24:72, gears 14:28, 16:26, 18:24, 21:24, 22:21, final 14:52; FC 450 primary 29:72, same gear ratios as the 350, final 13:51; all 5-speed with a DS clutch and Brembo hydraulics, 520 non-sealed chain.
notes: The FC 250 owner's manual lists a 14:52 final drive; the spec table says 14:51. See conflicts.

source.name: Cycle News - 2027 Husqvarna FC motocrossers specs and prices

statement: 2027 FC shared chassis: 25CrMo4 central double-cradle frame, polyamide/aluminium subframe, 48 mm WP XACT fork and XACT linkage shock with 305/293 mm travel, 26.1 degree head angle, 22 mm offset, 58.6 in wheelbase, 37.2 in seat, 13.2 in ground clearance, 1.9 gal tank; weights without fuel 224.2 lb (FC 250), 225.9 lb (FC 350), 227.7 lb (FC 450); US MSRP $10,799 / $11,199 / $11,749.

source.name: Cycle News - 2027 Husqvarna FC motocrossers specs and prices

statement: First-ride testers called the 2027 FC 250 the easiest bike in the Husqvarna range: good low-end torque, pulls out of corners even a gear too high, smooth and non-aggressive power, and soft suspension that stays calm over bumps at slower speeds.
notes: Qualitative impressions, no dyno figures.

source.name: InMoto.it - Test Husqvarna Cross 2027 (first ride, Cadrezzate)

statement: First-ride testers found the 2027 FC 450 the most demanding bike in the range: smooth off the first part of the throttle, then building strongly as the throttle opens, physically tiring without fitness, and less settled on rough ground unless ridden at a fast, committed pace.
notes: Qualitative impressions, no dyno figures.

source.name: InMoto.it - Test Husqvarna Cross 2027 (first ride, Cadrezzate)

statement: KTM lists three changes for the 2026 300 SX: a new fuel protector cap against outside damage and accidental opening, a threaded radiator cap that opens faster with less force, and new wiring-harness fixing points and routing to reduce wear and damage.

source.name: KTM USA model page - 2026 KTM 300 SX

statement: For 2026 the KTM SX range was restyled with mostly minor updates: a more uniform, easier radiator closure, a protector cap for the fuel quick-lock on fuel-injected models and re-routed two-stroke wiring harnesses that resist dirt intrusion; the full-size SX generation entered its fourth year. KTM's figure for the 300 SX is 219.1 lb without fuel.
notes: Magazine article relaying KTM's 2026 release.

source.name: Cycle News - New 2026 KTM SX and SX-F models specs

statement: KTM's 2026 250/300 SX owner's manual repeats the 2025 engine, gearing and chassis data; the visible change is the fork air table, now 10.0 / 10.2 / 10.4 bar for 65-75 / 75-85 / 85-95 kg riders instead of a single 10.2 bar standard.
notes: Comparison of the 2025 and 2026 manuals.

source.name: KTM Owner's Manual 2026 250 SX / 250 XC / 300 SX / 300 XC, item no. 3240233en (compared with 2025 manual 3240042en)

topic: 2026 SX two-stroke harness and fuel-coupling fixes
statement: KTM's 2026 updates address wear points on the TBI two-strokes: the wiring harness gets new fixing points and routing so it is less prone to wear and damage, and the fuel quick-lock coupling gets a protector cap against damage and accidental opening.
notes: Stated on the 2026 300 SX page; the range article applies the harness and cap changes to the SX two-strokes.

source.name: KTM USA model page - 2026 KTM 300 SX

statement: On a magazine the 2025 KTM 300 SX made 49.1 hp and 32.3 lb-ft at the rear wheel, about 1.3 hp less than KTM's 2025 350cc four-stroke motocrosser but about 5.7 lb-ft more torque.
notes: Applied to 2026 because KTM's 2026 changes were caps and harness only and the 2025 and 2026 owner's manuals list identical engine data.

source.name: Dirt Rider - How much power does the 2025 KTM 300 SX make? (Dynojet 250i)

statement: KTM describes the 2026 300 SX as Keihin EFI two-stroke with a reed case built for consistent power at any altitude and a power valve for usable power across the rev range; map 1 is linear and predictable, map 2 more aggressive.

source.name: KTM USA model page - 2026 KTM 300 SX

statement: The 2026 GasGas MC 450F changes are cosmetic: black rims and handlebar instead of silver and smaller logo graphics on the shrouds; the frame cut-outs (from 2025) and 45 N/mm shock spring (from 2024) carry over. US MSRP $10,499.
notes: Magazine technical overview; it lists 13.1:1 compression where the 2026 owner's manual lists 13.6:1 (see conflicts).

source.name: Dirt Rider - 2026 GasGas MC 450F Technical Overview

statement: A magazine measured the 2026 GasGas MC 450F at 53.4 hp at 10,100 rpm and 34.2 lb-ft at 7,200 rpm, with a 242 lb wet weight and a 37.5 in measured seat height.

source.name: Dirt Rider - 2026 GasGas MC 450F Technical Overview

statement: GasGas's 2027 MC 450F owner's manual repeats the 2026 technical data except the weight without fuel (103.0 to 103.6 kg), the chain printed as 520 and a single 51-tooth rear sprocket option listed.
notes: Comparison of the 2026 and 2027 manuals.

source.name: GASGAS Owner's Manual 2027 MC 450F, item no. 3215291en (compared with 2026 manual 3215269en)

statement: GasGas's 2027 MC 250F owner's manual repeats the 2026 technical data except: fork air now set by rider weight (10.1 / 10.3 / 10.5 bar for 65-75 / 75-85 / 85-95 kg; 2026 listed one 10.3 bar standard), weight 101.9 to 102 kg, chain printed as 520 and one 52-tooth rear sprocket listed.
notes: Comparison of the 2026 and 2027 manuals.

source.name: GASGAS Owner's Manual 2027 MC 250F, item no. 3215290en (compared with 2026 manual 3215268en)

statement: The 2020 TC 125 is the last carbureted TC 125 with the full 310/300 mm travel, 950 mm seat, WP XACT 5548 air fork at 8.3 bar (950 mm long) and one rectangular plus one half-keystone piston ring; 2021 lowered the bike (see 2021).
notes: Comparison of the 2020 and 2021 manuals.

source.name: Husqvarna Motorcycles Owner's Manual 2020 TC 125, item no. 3402332en (compared with the 2021 manual)

statement: Husqvarna's 2021 TC 125 manual versus 2020: travel cut to 300 mm front / 293 mm rear (from 310/300), seat 950 to 940 mm, fork changed to WP XACT 5448 (940 mm long) at 8.1 bar, new fork and shock part numbers, and two half-keystone piston rings.

source.name: Husqvarna Motorcycles Owner's Manual 2021 TC 125, item no. 3402439en (compared with the 2020 manual)

statement: Husqvarna's 2022 TC 125 manual repeats the 2021 technical data (Mikuni TMX 38 carburetor, kick start, 300/293 mm travel, 8.1 bar fork); 2022 is the last carbureted TC 125.

source.name: Husqvarna Motorcycles Owner's Manual 2022 TC 125, item no. 3402529en (compared with the 2021 manual)

statement: Husqvarna's 2023 TC 125 manual shows the new generation: the Mikuni carburetor gives way to throttle-body fuel injection, electric start replaces the kicker, weight without fuel rises from 87.8 to 92.6 kg, travel 305/293 mm, wheelbase 1,490 mm, ground clearance 375 to 350 mm, coolant 1.2 to 0.95 l, plug NGK BR10 ECMVX, and a new WP XACT fork (8.5 bar) and XACT shock with new part numbers and a 456.3 mm installed length.

source.name: Husqvarna Motorcycles Owner's Manual 2023 TC 125, item no. 3402629en (compared with the 2022 manual)

statement: Husqvarna's 2024 TC 125 manual versus 2023: fork renamed WP XACT AER with 8.3 bar standard pressure, shock now XACT LDS with 8 mm preload (was 7 mm), and new fork/shock part numbers; engine and chassis dimensions unchanged.

source.name: Husqvarna Motorcycles Owner's Manual 2024 TC 125, item no. 3402711en (compared with the 2023 manual)

statement: Husqvarna's 2025 TC 125 manual versus 2024: fork air 8.6 bar, final drive 13:50 (was 13:51), seat 946 mm (was 939), exhaust control start listed at 7,200 rpm, two half-keystone piston rings, 92 kg without fuel and new fork/shock part numbers; the same manual also covers the 150cc version.

source.name: Husqvarna Motorcycles Owner's Manual 2025 TC 125 / TC 150, item no. 3402801en (compared with the 2024 manual)

statement: Husqvarna's 2026 TC 125 manual repeats the 2025 TC 125 technical data apart from a 92.2 kg weight without fuel (92 kg in 2025).

source.name: Husqvarna Motorcycles Owner's Manual 2026 TC 125, item no. 3402882en (compared with the 2025 manual)

statement: The 2020 TC 250 is a carbureted (Mikuni TMX 38), kick-start bike with 310/300 mm travel, 950 mm seat and a 950 mm WP XACT 5548 air fork at 10.1 bar; 2021 lowered it.

source.name: Husqvarna Motorcycles Owner's Manual 2020 TC 250, item no. 3402333en (compared with the 2021 manual)

statement: Husqvarna's 2021 TC 250 manual versus 2020: travel 300/293 mm (from 310/300), seat 940 mm, WP XACT 5448 fork (940 mm) at 10.4 bar with fork rebound presets 23/18/13 clicks, shock high-speed presets 2.5/2/1.5 turns and rebound 17/15/13 clicks, new fork/shock part numbers.

source.name: Husqvarna Motorcycles Owner's Manual 2021 TC 250, item no. 3402440en (compared with the 2020 manual)

statement: Husqvarna's 2022 TC 250 manual versus 2021: fork back to a 950 mm length at 10.1 bar with rebound presets 17/12/7 clicks and fork oil volumes as in 2020, shock high-speed presets 2/1.5/1 turns; engine (Mikuni TMX 38, kick start) unchanged.

source.name: Husqvarna Motorcycles Owner's Manual 2022 TC 250, item no. 3402530en (compared with the 2021 manual)

statement: Husqvarna's 2023 TC 250 manual shows the new TBI generation: carburetor replaced by throttle-body fuel injection with electric start, primary 26:73 to 26:72, Z dimension 49.0 to 48.0 mm, plug NGK BR 8 ES, coolant 1.2 to 0.95 l, weight 96 to 99.6 kg, travel 305/293 mm, wheelbase 1,490 mm, ground clearance 375 to 346 mm, new WP XACT fork (940 mm, 10.5 bar) and XACT shock.

source.name: Husqvarna Motorcycles Owner's Manual 2023 TC 250 / TX 300, item no. 3402630en (compared with the 2022 manual)

statement: Husqvarna's 2024 TC 250 manual versus 2023: fork renamed WP XACT AER, shock XACT LDS with 8 mm preload (was 7), new fork/shock part numbers; engine and chassis data unchanged.

source.name: Husqvarna Motorcycles Owner's Manual 2024 TC 250 / TX 300, item no. 3402712en (compared with the 2023 manual)

statement: Husqvarna's 2025 TC 250 manual versus 2024: fork air 10.2 bar (was 10.5), seat 946 mm, 99.5 kg without fuel, new fork/shock part numbers; the same manual also covers the 300cc version (72 x 72 mm, 293.15 cc, 14:47 final drive).

source.name: Husqvarna Motorcycles Owner's Manual 2025 TC 250 / TC 300 / TX 300, item no. 3402802en (compared with the 2024 manual)

statement: Husqvarna's 2026 TC 250 manual repeats the 2025 TC 250 engine, gearing and chassis data.
notes: Comparison of the 2025 and 2026 manuals found no differences in the main technical data.

source.name: Husqvarna Motorcycles Owner's Manual 2026 TC 250 / TX 300, item no. 3402883en (compared with the 2025 manual)

statement: On a magazine the 2025 Husqvarna TC 250 (Heritage livery, mechanically identical to the standard bike) made 43.0 hp and 29.6 lb-ft at the rear wheel.
notes: Applied to 2026 because the 2025 and 2026 owner's manuals list the same engine data.

source.name: Dirt Rider - How much power does the 2025 Husqvarna TC 250 Heritage make? (Dynojet 250i)

source.name: Dirt Rider - How much power does the 2025 Husqvarna TC 150 make?

statement: GasGas's 2025 MC 125 manual versus 2024: fork air 8.6 bar (was 8.3), final drive 13:50, exhaust control start listed at 7,200 rpm, weight 93.1 to 92.3 kg, wheelbase 1,490 mm and new fork/shock part numbers; the manual now also covers the MC 150.

source.name: GASGAS Owner's Manual 2025 MC 125 / MC 150, item no. 3215219en (compared with 2024 manual 3215157en)

statement: GasGas's 2026 MC 125 manual repeats the 2025 engine and chassis data; the fork air is now given by rider weight (8.4 / 8.6 / 8.8 bar for 65-75 / 75-85 / 85-95 kg) and weight is 92.5 kg.

source.name: GASGAS Owner's Manual 2026 MC 125, item no. 3215266en (compared with 2025 manual 3215219en)

statement: GasGas's 2025 MC 250 manual versus 2024: fork named WP XACT AER at 10.2 bar (was 10.5), new fork/shock part numbers, engine and chassis data otherwise unchanged; the manual also covers the new MC 300.

source.name: GASGAS Owner's Manual 2025 MC 250 / MC 300 / EX 250 / EX 300, item no. 3215220en (compared with 2024 manual 3215158en)

statement: GasGas's 2026 MC 250 manual repeats the 2025 engine and chassis data; fork air is now listed by rider weight at 10.0 / 10.2 / 10.4 bar (the table prints the rider-weight bands as 65-75, 75-85 and 85-95).
notes: The 2026 manual prints the rider-weight bands in "bar" instead of kg, an obvious typo.

source.name: GASGAS Owner's Manual 2026 MC 250 / EX 300, item no. 3215267en (compared with 2025 manual 3215220en)

statement: KTM's 2025 150 SX manual versus the 2022 150 SX: the 144 cc engine (58 x 54.5 mm) is now fuel injected through a throttle body with electric start, where the 2022 bike used a Mikuni TMX 38 carburetor and kick start; the fork is now a WP XACT AER and the shock an XACT LDS, plug NGK BR10 ECMVX at 0.80 mm (was BR9 ECMVX at 0.60 mm), weight 87.5 to 92.1 kg, wheelbase 1,485 to 1,493 mm, seat 950 to 958 mm, ground clearance 375 to 359 mm.
notes: Comparison of the 150 SX sections of the 2022 and 2025 manuals.

source.name: KTM Owner's Manual 2025 125 SX / 125 XC / 150 SX, item no. 3240041en (compared with 2022 manual 3214411en)

statement: A dealer reported 2025 KTM 125 SX and 150 SX TBI bikes that would not start or fouled plugs; fixes that worked were cycling the fuel pump from the diagnostic tool, waiting for the handlebar light to go out before pressing start, and draining fuel mixed with cheap oil for fresh fuel with the specified 2-stroke oil. Suspected causes (injectors not holding pressure, fuel-pump leak, debris in the pump) were not confirmed.
notes: Single forum thread, four bikes, three posters; no KTM bulletin found.

source.name: Vital MX forum - 2025 KTM TBI starting issues

statement: Some 2023 KTM 250/300 SX TBI owners reported brief intermittent cut-outs under load or at idle that dealers could not reproduce; owners most often suspected the throttle position sensor or its pigtail, fuel pickup or a blocked fuel filter/tank vent. No recall, bulletin or confirmed fix was reported.
notes: About six posters; anecdotal.

source.name: Vital MX forum - 2023 KTM SX 250/300 stall / shut-off issue

statement: Yamaha's US owner's service manual for the 2021 WR250F identifies it as model WR250FM, model code BAK7; the manual is the US-market edition (Yamaha part BAK-2819U-11).

source.name: Yamaha 2021 WR250F Owner's Service Manual (BAK-2819U-11)

statement: The 2021 WR250F engine is a liquid-cooled 250 cm³ DOHC four-stroke single, bore × stroke 77.0 × 53.6 mm (3.03 × 2.11 in), compression ratio 13.8 : 1, electric start, wet-sump lubrication.

source.name: Yamaha 2021 WR250F Owner's Service Manual (BAK-2819U-11)

statement: Fuel injection with throttle body ID BAK1; fuel line pressure at idle 300–390 kPa (3.0–3.9 kgf/cm², 43.5–56.6 psi), idle speed 1900–2100 r/min; valve clearance (cold) intake 0.12–0.19 mm (0.0047–0.0075 in), exhaust 0.17–0.24 mm (0.0067–0.0094 in).

source.name: Yamaha 2021 WR250F Owner's Service Manual (BAK-2819U-11)

statement: Engine control unit BAK2; TCI ignition with timing 8.0–12.0 /2000 r/min; fuel pump and electronic fuel injection.

source.name: Yamaha 2021 WR250F Owner's Service Manual (BAK-2819U-11)

topic: 2021 WR250F maps, Power Tuner and launch control
statement: On the US 2021 WR250F there is no handlebar map switch; fuel and ignition can be adjusted only with the optional handheld GYTR Power Tuner (33D-H59C0-V1-00) plugged into the coupler provided.
notes: US manual. Other markets (e.g. Europe/Australia) may ship with the app and switch where the US bike lists only the optional a tuner.

source.name: Yamaha 2021 WR250F Owner's Service Manual (BAK-2819U-11)

statement: KYB coil-spring fork, 310 mm (12.2 in) travel, Yamaha Suspension Oil S1, 501.0 cm³ (16.94 US oz, 17.67 Imp.oz) per leg; standard clickers (counted out from fully in): rebound 8 of 20, compression 11 of 20.

source.name: Yamaha 2021 WR250F Owner's Service Manual (BAK-2819U-11)

statement: KYB link shock, 317 mm (12.5 in) wheel travel; standard settings: spring preload 7.0 mm (0.28 in) turned in from free length, rebound 11 clicks out (of 30), high-speed compression 1 turns out, low-speed compression 8 clicks out.

source.name: Yamaha 2021 WR250F Owner's Service Manual (BAK-2819U-11)

statement: Standard spring rates are 4.6 N/mm (fork) and None N/mm (shock); Yamaha lists optional fork springs from 4.1-5.1 N/mm. Rear sag is set to a sunken (rider-on) length of 90-100 mm before any other tuning.
notes: Spring tables in the Tuning chapter (front fork / rear shock absorber setting parts).

source.name: Yamaha 2021 WR250F Owner's Service Manual (BAK-2819U-11)

statement: Constant mesh 6-speed; primary reduction 3.353 (57/17); gear ratios 1st 2.385 (31/13), 2nd 1.813 (29/16), 3rd 1.444 (26/18), 4th 1.143 (24/21), 5th 0.957 (22/23), 6th 0.815 (22/27); secondary (final) reduction 3.923 (51/13), i.e. stock sprockets 13T front / 51T rear, chain final drive.

source.name: Yamaha 2021 WR250F Owner's Service Manual (BAK-2819U-11)

statement: Wet multi-disc clutch: 2 pcs friction plate 1 (2.70–2.90 mm), 6 pcs friction plate 2 (2.72–2.88 mm), 7 pcs clutch plate (1.50–1.70 mm); clutch spring free length 44.00 mm (1.73 in); 520 sealed type chain, 114 links, slack 50.0–60.0 mm (1.97–2.36 in). Yamaha lists optional rear sprockets of 48, 50, 51, 52 teeth.
notes: Plate counts are listed in manual order (friction plate types first, then clutch/steel plates).

source.name: Yamaha 2021 WR250F Owner's Service Manual (BAK-2819U-11)

topic: 2021 WR250F overall gear ratios and speed per 1,000 rpm
statement: Worked out from Yamaha's ratios, overall reduction (engine to rear wheel) is 1st 31.37:1, 2nd 23.85:1, 3rd 18.99:1, 4th 15.03:1, 5th 12.59:1, 6th 10.72:1; on the stock 110/100-18 rear tire that is about 1st 4.07 km/h, 2nd 5.35 km/h, 3rd 6.72 km/h, 4th 8.49 km/h, 5th 10.14 km/h, 6th 11.91 km/h per 1,000 rpm.
notes: overall = primary 3.353 x gear x secondary 3.923. Speed = rpm / overall x tire circumference; nominal rolling diameter 677 mm from 110/100-18 (rim x 25.4 + 2 x section x aspect), circumference 2.127 m, no tire squat or growth.

source.name: BAK calculation from Yamaha 2021 WR250F OSM ratios

statement: Worked out from Yamaha's gearbox and stock sprockets: first gear gives about 4.07 km/h and top gear about 11.91 km/h per 1,000 rpm, so at 10,000 rpm first runs out near 41 km/h and top near 119 km/h (74 mph). The ratio between first and top gear is 2.93, a measure of how wide the box is.
notes: Reference rpm 10000 chosen as a typical working rpm, not a published rev limit. Same tire assumptions as the drivetrain record.

source.name: BAK calculation from Yamaha 2021 WR250F OSM ratios

statement: Yamaha's tuning chart for this model says: set rear sag (sunken length 90-100 mm) first; if the fork is stiff over its whole range back the compression out about 2 clicks, take 5-10 cc of oil out or fit a softer spring; if it is soft and bottoms, add about 2 clicks of compression or 5-10 cc of oil, or fit a stiffer spring; change oil in 5 cc steps for end-of-stroke feel. topic: 2025 YZ250X overall gear ratios and speed per 1,000 rpm

statement: Yamaha's tuning chart for this model says: set rear sag (sunken length 90-100 mm) first; if the fork is stiff over its whole range back the compression out about 2 clicks, take 5-10 cc of oil out or fit a softer spring; if it is soft and bottoms, add about 2 clicks of compression or 5-10 cc of oil, or fit a stiffer spring; change oil in 5 cc steps for end-of-stroke feel. After a softer spring go 1-2 clicks out on rebound, after a stiffer one 1-2 clicks in.
notes: From the Tuning chapter (front fork setting / suspension setting tables) of this manual.

source.name: Yamaha 2027 YZ125 Owner's Service Manual (D68-2819U-12)

statement: The 2027 YZ125 engine is a liquid-cooled 125 cm³ two-stroke single, reed valve inducted, bore × stroke 54.0 × 54.5 mm (2.13 × 2.15 in), compression ratio 8.2–10.1 : 1 (Yamaha quotes a range; the higher figure corresponds to the power valve closed), kick start.

source.name: Yamaha 2027 YZ125 Owner's Service Manual (D68-2819U-12)

statement: Fuel is fed by a Keihin PWK38S carburetor (38 mm bore) through a reed valve with 0.400 mm (0.0157 in) thick reeds; lubrication is premix at 30:1 with Yamalube 2R.

source.name: Yamaha 2027 YZ125 Owner's Service Manual (D68-2819U-12)

statement: The 2027 YZ125 is carbureted (Keihin PWK38S), not fuel injected. Stock US jetting: id mark B4X3 20, main jet #178, main air jet #200, jet needle N3EW-2, needle jet 2.9 (#6), cutaway #7, pilot outlet 0.8, pilot jet #65, bypass 1 1.5, air screw turns out 1-3/8, valve seat size 3.8, starter jet 1 #85, power jet #95, float height 5.5 mm (0.22 in).
notes: US-market jetting from the spec table; Yamaha gives a jetting chart for temperature and altitude in the tuning chapter.

source.name: Yamaha 2027 YZ125 Owner's Service Manual (D68-2819U-12)

statement: Ignition is CDI with timing 0.53 mm (0.02 in) BTDC (piston position); the manual lists no handlebar map switch, engine-mode selector, traction control or Power Tuner connection for this model - power character is set by jetting, the CDI's fixed map and the mechanical YPVS power-valve governor.

topic: 2027 YZ125 overall gear ratios and speed per 1,000 rpm
statement: Worked out from Yamaha's ratios, overall reduction (engine to rear wheel) is 1st 30.28:1, 2nd 24.54:1, 3rd 20.16:1, 4th 17.17:1, 5th 14.93:1, 6th 13.4:1; on the stock 100/90-19 rear tire that is about 1st 4.12 km/h, 2nd 5.09 km/h, 3rd 6.2 km/h, 4th 7.27 km/h, 5th 8.37 km/h, 6th 9.32 km/h per 1,000 rpm.
notes: overall = primary 3.368 x gear x secondary 3.769. Speed = rpm / overall x tire circumference; nominal rolling diameter 663 mm from 100/90-19 (rim x 25.4 + 2 x section x aspect), circumference 2.082 m, no tire squat or growth.

source.name: BAK calculation from Yamaha 2027 YZ125 OSM ratios

statement: Worked out from Yamaha's gearbox and stock sprockets: first gear gives about 4.12 km/h and top gear about 9.32 km/h per 1,000 rpm, so at 11,000 rpm first runs out near 45 km/h and top near 103 km/h (64 mph). The ratio between first and top gear is 2.26, a measure of how wide the box is.
notes: Reference rpm 11000 chosen as a typical working rpm, not a published rev limit. Same tire assumptions as the drivetrain record.
